text:
maria: Heads-up — I hit an onboarding regression in the sample-kit when running the Node SDK in jsonMode + function-calls with strict schema validation. Node is returning a wrapped object for tool output while Py returns a bare array, validator refuses to accept it. Repro steps below.

alice: Can you paste a minimal repro and the exact validation error? Which SDK/runtime versions?

maria: Repro (quick):
1) git clone github.com/redwood/sample-kit && cd typed-output
2) yarn && yarn start --jsonMode
3) POST /generate with tool "extract_entities" whose parameters are an array (Entity[]).

Observed: node sdk's function call payload ends up with arguments like `{"result":[...]}` instead of the raw array. Py SDK emits the raw array. Schema validator throws "expected array, got object".

Example tool schema:
```json
{
  "name": "extract_entities",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "array",
    "items": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}
    }
  }
}
```

Console snippet:
```
sdk-node: returned 'arguments': {"result":[{"text":"Acme"}]}
schema-validator ERROR: expected array but got object at parameters
```

sam: I think this is the helper that coalesces multiple return slots — historically we wrapped multi-field returns into `{result: ...}` for older tool shapes. The Python helper kept raw arrays. Looks like a parity mismatch introduced in last SDK patch. Quick mitigation: normalize incoming args on the handler to accept both `array` and `{result: array}`.

rob: Can someone open an issue with a tiny failing test/fixture? I'll route to eng-ml for a parity fix. Also we should add an e2e in sample-kit to catch this.

ciara: I'll draft a PR to sample-kit that adds a small shim which accepts either shape and adds a fallback conversion. Also adding a tiny note in the onboarding doc about tool parameter shape expectations so new users aren't blocked.

sdk-bot: Note created: INF-2345 — "node-sdk: function-call argument wrapper mismatch in jsonMode" (assigned to @rob).

maria: Thanks. For the short term I'll apply the shim in our quickstart so onboarding doesn't fail for new signups. Long term we should pick a canonical shape (prefer raw arrays for parameters typed as arrays) and make both SDKs normalize on sending/receiving. Also suggest adding a CLI lint that warns when a tool schema declares array but sample handler expects object.

alice: :thumbsup: That plan sounds good. If you want I can pair on the e2e test later today.

maria: Appreciate it — marking INF-2345 as blocked on a small parity patch + sample-kit test.
